fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. He says he's like a drunkard "…because of the LORD, because of His holy words." (Jeremiah 23:9) I think that tells you how heavy those words are to carry. His heart is broken and his bones tremble, and the verse says it's because of the LORD and His holy words.

Yes, friend, you got it. The prophet says the land is full of adulterers, "…their course is evil and their power is misused." (Jeremiah 23:10) That's a heavy thing to hear. He's not hiding it, and I think that's why his heart is so broken.
Priest is right. The LORD says, "For both prophet and priest are ungodly…" (Jeremiah 23:11) Both of them, together. The prophet and the priest are named in the same breath.
Field is a fun guess, but it's not in the verse. The LORD says He found their wickedness "even in My house…" (Jeremiah 23:11) Not in a field, in His house. That's what makes it so serious.

False, and you got it. The LORD says the prophets "…strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns his back on wickedness." (Jeremiah 23:14) Nobody turns his back on it, and I think that's the whole problem here. The people are staying right where they are.
Sodom is right. The LORD says, "They are all like Sodom to Me; the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah." (Jeremiah 23:14) Two cities named together, and it's a heavy comparison.

That's the reason. The LORD says, "…for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has spread throughout the land." (Jeremiah 23:15) It spread from them across the land. Wormwood and poisoned water are the heavy consequence He names for it.

That would be a warning, and that's not the message the passage reports. The LORD says they tell the stubborn, "No harm will come to you." (Jeremiah 23:17) Nothing about turning back there. That's the message they keep repeating.
That's not what they say, friend. The LORD says they tell the stubborn, "No harm will come to you." (Jeremiah 23:17) The words the passage reports are just smooth, comfy ones.

Fire is not the word here, baker. The LORD says, "…the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked." (Jeremiah 23:19) It's a storm, and it's described as a whirlwind. Not a fire.

Right. The LORD says, "…if they had stood in My council, they would have proclaimed My words to My people and turned them back from their evil ways and deeds." (Jeremiah 23:22) Standing in His council is where proclaiming His words would have come from. And turning His people back is what He says they would have done.
